title: Robustness batch from the 1.4.6 review: callback-NULL class, simulator alloc check, address-string buffer contract, console RNG docs
body:
Robustness hardening batch from the v1.4.6 security review. None is reachable from unauthenticated network input (independently verified); all are local API-misuse or test-path robustness. Grouping them for one small, wire-neutral PR.

**1. Callback-NULL class (setup-time validation closes it).** Two config callbacks are called without a NULL guard:
- `send_loopback_packet_callback` — `netcode.c:3534` (client, no assert) and `:5255` (server, assert-only). A loopback connection with the callback unset crashes release builds.
- `receive_packet_override` — `netcode.c:3263` (client) and `:5039` (server), invoked under `override_send_and_receive` with no NULL check on the pointer, so it crashes in debug *and* release. Its twin `send_packet_override` *is* checked at `:2768`.

Fix (preferred): validate at create time — if `override_send_and_receive` is set, require both override callbacks non-NULL; document that a loopback client/server must set `send_loopback_packet_callback`. One check in each create path closes the whole class. (Call-site NULL guards are the lighter alternative.)

**2. Network simulator: unchecked allocation** — `netcode.c:2630-2631`. `memcpy` into the result of `allocate_function` with no NULL check; the only unchecked config allocation in the file. Test/simulator path only. Fix: NULL-check and drop the packet.

**3. `netcode_address_to_string` buffer contract** — `NETCODE_MAX_ADDRESS_STRING_LENGTH` is defined in `netcode.c:50`, not in `netcode.h`, so a public-header-only caller cannot name the required buffer size. Internal writes truncate (snprintf/inet_ntop), so no overflow inside. Fix: move the constant to `netcode.h`, document the contract on the function; keep the signature (ports mirror it).

**4. Console RNG (docs)** — on `__ORBIS__`/`__PROSPERO__` the vendored sodium `randombytes_sysrandom_buf` never writes the buffer (upstream semantics), so keys come from uninitialised memory. Document in `sodium/NOTES.md` / IMPLEMENTERS that a console port must register a real RNG via `randombytes_set_implementation`.

Not changing: negative `timeout_seconds` (STANDARD.md:45 documents "negative values disable timeout (dev only)"; rides inside the AEAD-sealed token, not network-reachable) and connection-response type-3 nonce reuse (conformant to STANDARD.md:308-312; degrades only the attacker's own session).

Full audit and per-finding verification are private (mas-bandwidth/security#24). No wire-format change in any of the above; GATE on licensing untouched.
